title: Latency pipeline bridge + trace-map for model/route (stream vs non-stream)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Engineers and Product need a single-pane view that ties percentile latency (p50/p95/p99) to traces and to a streaming vs non-streaming request split across model + route. Current dashboards show percentiles but lack trace attribution and the streaming/non-stream toggle. The runtime now emits a stream_flag and kv_cache_hit on request metadata, but our metrics pipeline drops that context during histogram aggregation. This ticket implements a "pipeline bridge" to preserve request-level tags through histogram ingest and adds a Trace Map dashboard that surfaces tail traces correlated with percentile spikes by model and route.

Goals:
- Ensure percentiles by model + route are computed with streaming/non-stream dimension preserved (p50/p95/p99).
- Add trace-hooks in the serving runtime to attach a short trace_id and metadata (model, route, streaming_flag, kv_cache_hit, batch_size) to logs/metrics for 95% of requests and full traces sampled for 1% (configurable).
- Build a Grafana dashboard (Trace Map) that shows: percentile sparkline, % of requests streaming vs non-streaming, heatmap of tail latency cohorts, and list of representative traces with links to Jaeger/Tempo.
- Implement migration plan to switch dashboards with no user-visible regressions and instrument alerting for pipeline regressions.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Sampling: use adaptive sampling to increase trace capture during p95/p99 regressions to avoid missing root causes; default 1% global, ramp to 10% on percentile breach. Trade-off: increased tracing cost vs faster RCA on incidents.
- Metrics pipeline layering: implement a short-lived Kafka topic "latency-bridge-v2" where enriched metric events (with stream_flag, model, route) are replayed into the histogram-aggregator. This avoids changing the core aggregator immediately. Trade-off: transient complexity vs safer rollout.
- Histogram buckets: add finer buckets around 50-1000ms to better resolve p50 and p95 for short-models. Rolling change to buckets requires re-indexing for older data; we will keep previous buckets for historical continuity and only apply new buckets moving-forward.

Instrumentation details (runtime changes):
- Add trace_hook to runtime request path: add short trace_id (8 hex chars), attach tags: model, route, io_mode (streaming|blocking), kv_cache_hit (true|false), batch_size. Emit an enriched metric event to latency-bridge-v2 topic containing request_id, trace_id, latency_ms, status_code, tags.
- Logging: emit single-line JSON log with these tags at request-completion for sampleable requests.
- Metrics: histogram event includes the tags; aggregator will compute p50/p95/p99 by (model, route, io_mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- New dashboard includes p50/p95/p99 lines split by io_mode and a heatmap of tail cohorts, with trace links for at least 95% of sampled anomalies.
- Enriched events appear in latency-bridge-v2 topic within 200ms of request completion in staging.
- No more than 5% increase in overall metrics ingestion costs in staging at default sampling.
- Runbook updated with how to interpret Trace Map and how to trigger increased trace sampling.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement runtime trace_hook behind feature flag (runtime.flag.latency_trace_map). 2) Deploy bridge consumer in staging to consume latency-bridge-v2 and feed aggregator. 3) Run for 2 full days and compare percentiles to existing pipeline (diff < 2% at p50/p95). 4) Enable adaptive sampling in staging and verify trace links populate dashboard. 5) Gradual production rollout (10% clusters -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback flag.

Rollback criteria:
- If p95 changes > 5% vs baseline or aggregator lag > 5s for more than 10 minutes, immediately disable bridge consumer and feature flag.

Risks / open questions:
- Need confirmation from storage team on retention impact of a higher tracing sample rate (opens ticket STORAGE-298).
- Dashboard performance: the dashboard will query both metrics store and trace storage; we need to validate query latency under peak.
